sentences.text:
Heard Shri Ramesh Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the appellant - Meerut Development Authority.

2. The instant first appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been filed by the Meerut Development Authority against the award and decree dated 15.03.2003 passed by the Court of District Judge, Meerut in LAR No. 171 of 1992, Dharam Pal v. State of U.P. and others, whereby for the acquired land situated in Village Nagla Tasi, Kasimpur, District Meerut, compensation at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been awarded to the land owners.

entities.text: Dharam Pal v. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that for the similarly situated acquired land, the Apex Court in the case of Meharban and others vs. State of U.P. and others, reported in AIR 1997 SC 2664 and this Court in First Appeal No. 1013 of 2004, Meerut Development Authority vs. Khubi and others, and in other connected appeals and also in First Appeal (Defective) No. 412 of 2003, Meerut Development Authority v. Omvir Singh and others, connected with 24 other first appeals by orders dated 16.02.2016 and 10.05.2016 respectively has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard, which is same as has been awarded by the Reference Court.

entities.text: Meharban and others vs. State of U.P. and others, reported in AIR 1997 SC 2664
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Meerut Development Authority vs. Khubi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Meerut Development Authority v. Omvir Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the appeal be disposed of in the light of the above-referred judgements of the Apex Court and of this Court.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant- Meerut Development Authority and perused the record.

5. It is apparent that in this case, the landowners acquired land is situated in Village Nagla Tasi,
Kasimpur, District Meerut which was acquired for the benefit of the Meerut Development Authority vide notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 14.08.1987, regarding which the Award of the Collector was made on 22.02.1990 whereby compensation at the rate of Rs. 50/- per sq. yard was awarded, besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The order of Collector was challenged by the landowners by filing Reference which has been allowed by the impugned Award and Decree whereby, compensation at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard,
besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been awarded to the landowners.

6. It is apparent that the Apex Court in the case of Meharban and others (supra) has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard for similarly situated and acquired land of other landowners, which has been followed by this Court in First Appeal No. 1013 of 2004, Meerut M.D.A. vs Dharmpal on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100885374/
1 Development Authority vs. Khubi and others, connected with six other first appeals and also in First Appeal (Defective) No. 412 of 2003, Meerut Development Authority vs. Omvir Singh and others,
connected with 24 other first appeals wherein by orders dated 16.02.2016 and 10.05.2016 respectively, this Court has also awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard for similarly situated acquired land in Village Nagla Tasi, Kasimpur, District Meerut.
7.

entities.text: Meerut M.D.A. vs Dharmpal on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Development Authority vs. Khubi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Meerut Development Authority vs. Omvir Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the Reference Court has awarded compensation for the acquired land at the rate of Rs. 175/-
per sq. yard which is similar to the compensation awarded by the Apex Court in the case of Meharban and others (supra) and this Court in First Appeal No. 1013 of 2004 and First Appeal (Defective) No. 412 of 2003 with other connected appeals, as such, the instant appeal which seeks reduction of the amount of compensation awarded by the Reference Court, is not maintainable.
8. In view of the above pronouncement of the Apex Court and this Court, the compensation awarded by the Reference Court at the rate of Rs. 175/- per sq. yard cannot be reduced any further.
9. Accordingly, the instant appeal is meritless and is hereby dismissed.
The impugned Decree and Award of the lower court dated 15.03.2003 is hereby affirmed.
10. However, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the parties shall bear there own costs.
11. Office is directed to prepare the decree accordingly.

(Sandeep Jain,J.) September 4, 2025 Rama Kant  M.D.A. vs Dharmpal on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100885374/
